display.title: Ki Sisa: Lift Up the Head, Lift Up Shabbos
display.summary_short: Hidden in the opening words of Parshas Ki Sisa is a secret: lift each letter of 'rosh' one step in the aleph-beis and it spells Shabbos, the head of the Jewish people.
display.summary_long: A parsha talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi explains 'Baruch Hashem, here we are': every day is a new chance to go higher in holiness. Parshas Ki Sisa opens with Moshe Rabbeinu counting everyone over twenty by the half-shekel. But the Torah is Hashem's own, written in Loshon HaKodesh, the holy language with which Hashem created the world, and it holds hidden secrets. 'Ki sisa es rosh' means 'when you lift up the head': lift each letter of rosh (reish, aleph, shin) one step higher in the aleph-beis and you get shin, beis, sav, Shabbos. Shabbos is the head of the Jewish people, and the Sages teach that if we kept two Shabbosos properly we would be redeemed at once. Since Shabbos comes every week and has so many laws, the 'order of the day' for Tzivos Hashem soldiers is to ask their teacher to set aside time each week for practical laws of Shabbos, to bring Moshiach now.
display.lesson: Lift up Shabbos and you lift up the whole Jewish people: learn the laws of Shabbos every week.
